# Case 232: Factory Ownership Convention Changed

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Verdict** | ✅ **NO_CHANGE** |
| **Category** | No Change |
| **Classification** | Rule |
| **Platforms** | Linux |

| **Detected `ChangeKind`s** | — |
| **Source files** | `catalog/cases/case232_factory_ownership_convention_changed/` |
| **Rule family** | [`factory-ownership-convention-changed`](by-rule/factory-ownership-convention-changed.md) |
| **Subject** | [Behavioral breaks outside static evidence](by-subject/behavioral-breaks-outside-static-evidence.md) |

**Category:** No Change (declared interface) | **Verdict:** ✅ NO_CHANGE — with a separate **behavioral break**

## Verdict and consumer impact

`ui::make_widget(int)` keeps its declaration, symbol, the `Widget` layout
and the library's imports. Only the ownership of the returned raw pointer
changes: v1 returns a new object per call that the caller owns and
deletes; v2 caches one widget per id and keeps ownership. Old consumers
now share state they believe is private, and their `delete` frees memory
the library still uses (double free, use after free).

This is a **behavioral break**, not a source (API) or binary (ABI) break. As
a statement about the declared interface the verdict is `NO_CHANGE`, and that
stays true even with build data and sources (see below). The break is
recorded in `ground_truth.json` as `behavioral_break: true` with
`truth_scope: declared-interface`.

## Old/new diff

| v1.cpp | v2.cpp |
|--------|--------|
| `return new Widget{id, 1};` | `static Widget *cache[64]; ... return slot;` (library-owned) |

`v1.h` and `v2.h` are identical.

## abicheck command

```bash
g++ -shared -fPIC -g v1.cpp -o libv1.so
g++ -shared -fPIC -g v2.cpp -o libv2.so
abicheck compare libv1.so libv2.so --header old=v1.h --header new=v2.h
```

## Expected abicheck finding

```text
Compatibility: NO_CHANGE | Policy: strict_abi | Gate: ACCEPTED (exit 0)
Findings: 0 detected; 0 retained (0 gating, 0 non-gating); 0 review groups.
```

No `ChangeKind` is expected. The absence is the detection control; the
behavioral regression is recorded separately.

## Minimum evidence

`min_evidence: L2`. The public header AST is what establishes that the
*published* declaration is unchanged. Nothing deeper adds a fact: the case
was also compared at `--depth source` with `compile_commands.json` and both
source trees, and the result is still `NO_CHANGE`.

## Why abicheck reports nothing

abicheck's deterministic checks compare what the artifacts *declare*:
exported symbols, DWARF types and layout, header declarations, build flags,
and source-graph dependencies. All of those are identical here. The change
sits in an out-of-line function body, and its meaning (who owns the object behind a raw `Widget*`) exists only in
documentation. No static rule can tell a bug fix from a contract break in a
function body, so abicheck correctly does not guess. That is why
`ground_truth.json` records `truth_scope: declared-interface` and a separate
`behavioral_break: true`: **`NO_CHANGE` here does not mean "safe to ship".**
See [Behavioral & Semantic Compatibility](../../learn/behavioral-compatibility.md).

## Runtime failure demonstration

**Severity: an unchanged old consumer breaks at runtime; no static tool shows
it.**

```bash
g++ -shared -fPIC -g v1.cpp -o libv1.so
g++ -g app.cpp -L. -lv1 -Wl,-rpath,'$ORIGIN' -o app
./app            # a=0x...2b0 b=0x...2d0 b->value=1               exit 0
g++ -shared -fPIC -g v2.cpp -o libv1.so   # swap in v2, no recompile
./app            # a=0x...2d4 b=0x...2d4 b->value=5
                 # WRONG RESULT: widgets are shared, not caller-owned  exit 1
```

## Safe redesign

Put ownership in the type. Return `std::unique_ptr<Widget>` for a
caller-owned object, or `std::shared_ptr<Widget>` / a reference for a
library-owned one. Switching between them changes the return type, which
abicheck reports. Replacing the exported factory's return type in place is
itself an ABI break, so add a differently named typed factory or make the
change in an ABI-major release. With a raw pointer, add a new function (`get_widget(id)`)
for the cached object and keep `make_widget` allocating.

## Cross-tool comparison

`abidiff` and ABICC also report no change: they compare the same symbols,
types and declarations. Catching this break needs a test that runs a consumer
against the new library (the `app.cpp` above is such a test).

---

## Ground-truth provenance

**Behavioral break:** Not a compatibility claim for the release. A static comparison at every evidence depth (binary, headers, build data, sources) sees the same declaration, the same symbol and the same layout, so NO_CHANGE is the truth only for the declared interface. The runtime witness breaks a valid old consumer: app.cpp creates two widgets for one id and edits one; against v1 they are independent (exit 0), against v2 both pointers are the same shared object (exit 1), and the consumer's delete would free library-owned memory. A raw Widget* carries no ownership, so no deterministic detector can see the change.
